question.text: A ball is thrown horizontally with a speed of 20 m/s from a point O at the top edge of a wedge-shaped incline. Point Q lies directly beneath O, and the sloped surface of the wedge falls away at 45° to the horizontal. The ball follows a curved path and lands on the sloped surface at point P, where the angle OPQ equals 45°.

parts.label: a
parts.asks: Find the flight time of the ball before it lands on the sloped surface at P.

parts.label: b
parts.asks: Find the straight-line distance OP that the ball covers from launch to landing on the slope.

conditions: ball launched horizontally with speed 20 m/s from point O
point Q lies directly below O
the incline (and angle OPQ) makes 45° with the horizontal
ball lands on the incline at point P

figure.description: O is the launch point at the top of a right-angled wedge; Q lies directly below O. The sloped face of the wedge runs down toward the base, meeting the horizontal base at 45°. The ball's curved path from O meets the slope at P, and the angle OPQ between line OP and the horizontal line QP is 45°.

solution.approach: On a 45° incline, the vertical drop equals the horizontal distance travelled, so equate them to find the time, then find OP from the two legs.

steps.text: Write the horizontal distance and the vertical drop as functions of time for the horizontal launch, taking g = 10 m/s².
The particle lands on the incline where the drop equals the horizontal distance, because the incline makes 45° with the horizontal.
steps.why_this_step: On a 45° incline through O, every point has its vertical drop equal to its horizontal distance from O.

steps.text: Solve this equation for the time of flight (part a).
Find the horizontal distance and the vertical drop at t = 4 s.
OP is the straight-line distance from O to P, the hypotenuse of the right triangle with legs x = 80 m and y = 80 m.

common_mistakes.text: Taking the range OP as the horizontal distance 80 m instead of the slanted distance along the incline, missing the factor √2.
Writing the vertical drop as g t² instead of ½ g t², which gives t = 2 s and OP = 40√2 m ≈ 56.6 m.
